description:
FILED s464aw while shipping #972, probed 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl AFTER #972.

TWO faults, one mechanism -- a compound assignment does not consult its own
overload key and four of them do not consult ANY key, because
`%define-compound-pair' inlines the arithmetic instead of delegating to the
base-op function that owns the dispatch.

=== (a) FOUR COMPOUND OPS HAVE NO DISPATCH AT ALL ===

    package B1; use overload q/*/=>sub{"MUL"}, q/%/=>sub{"MOD"},
                             q/./=>sub{"CAT"}, q/x/=>sub{"REP"},
                             q(0+)=>sub{42}, q("")=>sub{"B1"};
    $z = B1->new;
    $z *= 3     perl MUL   PCL 126
    $z %= 3     perl MOD   PCL 0
    $z .= 3     perl CAT   PCL B13
    $z x= 3     perl REP   PCL B1B1B1

`p-*=' emits `(* (to-number CUR) (to-number VAL))', `p-%=' `(mod (truncate
...))', `p-.=' `(concatenate 'string (to-string ...))', `p-str-x=' its own
repeat -- none of them reaches `p-*' / `p-%' / `p-.' / `p-str-x', which are
where the dispatch lives.  (`+=' and `-=' DO delegate, through
`%p-compound-+-slow'; `/=' and `**=' delegate; `&=' `|=' `^=' delegate; `<<='
and `>>=' were made to delegate by #972, which also fixed the clamp they had
lost by being a second copy.)  Note that `x' has NO overload dispatch even in
its NON-compound form -- see #1005.

THE FIX IS THE DELEGATION, and it is four lines, but it is on the hot
compound path: measure the bench before and after (`*=' currently avoids a
notinline call to `p-*').  If the delegation costs, the alternative is a
guarded slow path like `%compound-arith-form''s.

=== (b) THE COMPOUND SPELLING IS LOST BEFORE `nomethod' SEES IT ===

perl passes `nomethod' the COMPOUND operator name and marks the call a
MUTATOR by passing undef as the third argument:

    package NM1; use overload q(0+)=>sub{7}, q("")=>sub{"NM1"},
                              nomethod=>sub{"NM[$_[3]/sw=".(defined $_[2]?"D":"U")."]"};
    $x -= 1     perl NM[-=/sw=U]    PCL NM[-/sw=D]
    $x |= 2     perl NM[|=/sw=U]    PCL NM[|/sw=D]

because PCL reaches the dispatch through `%p-compound---slow' -> `p--', which
by then only knows `-'.  The same loss is why #960(a)'s refusal message will
say `Operation "-"' where perl says `Operation "-="'.

perl also consults a DEDICATED compound key when the class declares one:

    package C2; use overload q/|=/ => sub {"ORASSIGN2"}, q(0+)=>sub{42};
    my $z = C2->new; $z |= 3;    perl ORASSIGN2   PCL 43

and refuses with `Operation "="' when the target is SHARED and the class has
no `=' copy constructor (probed) -- that last part is the `=' key, task #1006.

BAR: the eight probe rows above; the sweep (a `cl/' change); bench A/B for
half (a); guards in Pl/t/overload-01.t.

=== HALF (a) DONE (s470bk); half (b) NOT DONE ===
HALF (a) FIXED, runtime-only, one commit with #1005's `x` half.
`*=` `%=` `.=` `x=` reached NO overload dispatch because each INLINED its own
arithmetic instead of delegating to the base operator that owns it.  Rule 11,
one builder: `%compound-arith-form` â the guarded delegation `+=`/`-=` have
used since #900 â gains a form-BUILDER alternative to its `cl-op` symbol (for
`%`, `.` and `x`, whose plain arm is not a single CL operator), plus three
one-line out-of-line slow halves beside `%p-compound-+-slow`.  `x=` delegates
outright, like `/=` does.  `x` itself got its handler lookup in the same commit
(#1005's `x` half) so `x=` has something to delegate to.

A SECOND BUG IN THE SAME COPY: `x=`'s inlined body was
`(apply #'concatenate 'string (make-list N :initial-element â¦))`, the exact
spelling task #880 removed from `p-str-x` because it passes N ARGUMENTS to
CONCATENATE â `$s x= 200000` exhausted the control stack while
`$s = $s x 200000` was fine.  Not observable at the gate's 512 MB stack
(probed), dead in any runner with a small one.

MEASURED: 21 rows one file, byte-identical to perl 5.40.3 â the four compound
ops, the four non-compound, the SWAPPED `3 x $obj`, a class with only `""`
(whose `.`/`x` answers must NOT move, and do not), and seven plain-path rows.

THE SPEED COST THE TASK ASKED FOR, measured and filed as #1153:
`for (1..4e6) { $n *= 3; $n %= 1000003 }` (emitted `p-*=-raw`/`p-%=-raw`),
best-of-5 interleaved, PCL startup measured separately at 0.157 s â
process 0.172 -> 0.188 s (+9.4 %), the LOOP alone 0.015 -> 0.031 s (roughly
doubled), perl 0.111 s total / 0.106 s of loop, so PCL still beats perl there
3.4x where it beat it 7x.  `.=` is UNCHANGED (the `str-buffer` Kind-A emission
owns the hot string path and never reaches `p-.=`).
THE TEST ORDER WAS RE-TRIED AND REVERTED: box-test-before-flag read 0.1859 s
against 0.1893 s, inside both spreads, so #972's five-candidate table stands
and the attempt's numbers are left in `%compound-arith-form`'s comment.  DO NOT
re-try it without a better instrument.

HALF (b) NOT DONE: the COMPOUND operator name reaching `nomethod`
(`Operation "-="`, and the mutator marker undef as the third argument) and the
dedicated compound KEY (`q/|=/`).  It needs the compound spelling threaded
through `%p-compound-*-slow` -> the base op -> `%p-nomethod-binary`, which the
current shape throws away by construction, and it is entangled with #1006(a)
(the `=` copy constructor) as that task says.  Corpus exposure is zero
(`nomethod` in NO file of the four populations).

Guard `Pl/t/overload-01.t` rows 36-37, inverse-verified on a `92a568e`
worktree; row 37 carries the negatives and passes both ways by design.
subject: the compound-assignment family: four ops have NO overload dispatch, and the rest report the BASE operator
